|---|---|---|---|---|

Tracks: A — Collection interval and revision size (research). B — Budget, staffing and attrition (research). Split from A because A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly, while B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built, and B's answer does not change A's model.

Track order: A, then B (partner's ranking).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision size
      Objective: Estimate, on real total-nonfarm vintages, how the scale of the one-month revision moves with collection days before first release.
      Outcomes: O1
      Track: A
      Consumes: nothing (the package is a scaffold with smoke tests)
      Produces: A real monthly vintage panel of first and second prints with a collection-days covariate from the release calendar, a first fitted model of one-month revision scale, and specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md reports the estimated relation between collection days and one-month revision scale over the full available vintage span, with its uncertainty; it records the measured cost of the real run: time to assemble the calendar and vintages, panel data volume, and wall-clock time of the fit.
      Leaves out: vintage-panel provenance manifest (Ranked list A, item 3); full validation suite (Ranked list A, item 4)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Sample size, attrition and revision size
      Objective: Estimate, on real data, how revision scale moves with CES sample size and sample attrition.
      Outcomes: O6
      Track: B
      Consumes: Stage 1's vintage panel and revision measures (plan <id>, Handoff, once Stage 1 completes)
      Produces: Hand-built monthly or annual sample-size and attrition series joined to the vintage panel, a fitted model of revision scale on them, and specs/ces-revisions-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: specs/ces-revisions-stage-2-findings.md reports the estimated relation between sample size, attrition and revision scale, with its uncertainty and a plain statement of what the slow-moving variation can and cannot identify; it records the measured cost of the real run: time to hand-build the series, and wall-clock time of the fit.
      Leaves out: covariate traceability (Ranked list B, item 3); full validation suite (Ranked list A, item 4)
      ROUTING: brainstorming
